A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlashBias research and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original efficiency and accuracy experiments for Transformers, GPT-2, SwinV2, PDE solving, AlphaFold 3, and Pangu-Weather, plus bias-reconstruction analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results, revises several measurements, and adds backend comparisons, an optimized ALiBi comparison, and AlphaFold component timings.

M1.justification: V2 adds a proposed multiplicative-bias procedure that repeats and reweights queries and keys into CR channels (Appendix I), extending beyond v1's additive-bias concatenation. SwinV2 acceleration changes from selected heads in most layers to the final eight layers, and Appendix C introduces JIT generation of ALiBi factors. The three original additive decomposition schemes remain.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage remains GPT-2/ALiBi, ImageNet-1K/SwinV2, car-simulation PDE solving, PDB protein folding, ERA5 weather forecasting, and synthetic gravity and spherical biases. The new backend tests change configurations within existing coverage; multiplicative bias receives mathematical treatment without an added empirical task.

E2.justification: V2 adds an explicitly evaluated FlashAttention ALiBi_slopes comparator in Appendix C, which was absent from v1's ALiBi comparisons. Figure 5 also explicitly compares FlashBias implementations against PyTorch SDPA with a bias matrix. Existing main-table comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: SwinV2 changes from head subsets with layer-specific ranks to the last eight layers with R=16. AlphaFold factor rank increases from 64 to 96, output width from 256 to 384, and reported fine-tuning from 2,000 to 10,000 iterations, retaining the PDB splits. The new backend comparison introduces a 128-channel, eight-head, R=8 configuration and TFLOPs/s measurement.

E4.justification: V2 adds a training-versus-inference backend comparison (Figure 5), an ALiBi JIT implementation comparison (Appendix C), and an AlphaFold component-level bottleneck analysis (Table 9). It revises Swin rank analysis from maxima within head subsets to maximum and mean ranks across heads, and changes the SVD reconstruction case. The existing AlphaFold reconstruction analysis is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: V2's checklist newly reports timing differences below 0.01 seconds per 100 iterations across experimental rounds and fixed memory usage, extending v1's qualitative stability statement. Both versions retain averaging over 1,000 iterations; no independent-run count, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Under revised configurations, Swin FlashBias top-1 accuracy changes from 87.126% to 87.186% and memory from 5,484 to 9,429 MB (Table 4). AlphaFold FlashBias/official-code memory changes from 10.37/21.58 to 13.62/13.62 GB, eliminating the reported inference-memory advantage (Table 6). Training-efficiency results also change. New results include identical optimized ALiBi timings of 119.8 seconds training and 38.98 seconds inference per 100 iterations. These revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix I adds a formal multiplicative-bias definition, factorization identity, cosine-bias example, and an HBM-complexity corollary with proof. Appendix J adds a low-rank-plus-sparse optimization formulation as a possible future remedy. The original main theorems and Appendix A proofs are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the 1.5-times speedup claim from AlphaFold generally to Pairformer in AlphaFold 3. The introduction's contribution bullet still uses broader AlphaFold wording, while the central low-rank acceleration contributions and conclusion remain essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for biases that are not low rank and proposes an unimplemented sparse correction (Appendix J). It adds explanations of token-wise factor functions and RoPE's existing computational compatibility. It also removes v1's interpretation that AlphaFold acceleration approaches the bias-free efficiency bound.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's PyTorch, hardware, and fine-tuning documentation, v2 specifies Triton 3.0.0, Triton inference versus SDPA training, and JIT factor construction. It documents revised layer/rank settings and increases the stated AlphaFold fine-tuning time from about five to ten hours. V2 also newly announces FlashBias code availability and supplies a repository address.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Triton and Chandrasekaran et al.'s sparse-and-low-rank decomposition work. It expands positioning relative to the already-cited RoPE and acknowledges FlashAttention's specialized ALiBi support. The broader compressed-sensing and attention-acceleration positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, targeted explanatory paragraphs are inserted, and the existing neural-decomposition discussion moves into Section 4.4. Acknowledgments, a NeurIPS checklist, and additional appendix sections are added, but most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 5 and Tables 8–9, redraws the Swin rank plot, and expands its SVD visualization from eight to sixteen heads. The existing AlphaFold bias visualization moves into the main text, and Figures 3–4 are rendered more sharply with retained trends. These are localized display changes within the existing document format.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through the optimized ALiBi comparison showing equal speed, explicit backend choices, code-access information, and clearer applicability limits. The narrower abstract and revised AlphaFold discussion better match the reported evidence. These benefits are tempered by a new mathematical inconsistency: Example I.3's R <= 27 does not follow from Corollary I.2's square-root bound for C=64 and S=100 KB. The core evidence remains largely retained, supporting a limited overall improvement.
